value.body:
Clocks, Jack Heart, quoting back "any keyword on run.log is a clock, so the first row that uses it declares it / it's a count unless you declare it Time / its name is its label / a later row missing it is refused": "these all sound fine to me" (and earlier: "why would you need to pass seconds if we already have the two built ins"). So: clocks are declared by use: run.steps declares its counted clock; the first run.log keyword declares any other, as a count, labelled by its name; a later row missing a used clock is refused (strict) or warned. Remove Step(...) from the public API (warning alias if released) and make track(clocks=) optional; keep Time(...) only as an optional declaration for a custom seconds clock; running_hours and hours_since_start stay built in. Old run.json clock declarations stay readable. Words in scratch/demo-hanabi.md.
